statement.p: Calculate the average height above the x-axis of a point in the region 0\le x\le a, 0\le y \le x^2

static.solution:
( x,y ) in the region \mathcal{D} above the x-axis is f( x,y )=y.
Therefore, the average height is the following value:
\overline{H}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{Area} (\mathcal{D})}\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} y \,dA We first compute the integral.
The region \mathcal{D} is a vertically simple region defined by the inequalities 0\le x\le 13 ,\quad 0\le y\le {x}^2
Therefore, \begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} y \,dA \amp =\amp \int_0^{13} \int_0^{{x}^2} y \,dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^{13} \frac{1}{2}{y}^2\bigg|_{y=0}^{{x}^2} \,dx= \int_0^{13} \frac{1}{2}\left({x}^4-0\right) \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^{13} \frac{1}{2}{x}^4 \,dx= \frac{{x}^5}{10}\bigg|_0^{13}=\frac{13^5}{10} \end{array} We compute the area of \mathcal{D} using the formula for the area as a double integral:
\begin{array}{rcl} \mathrm{Area} (\mathcal{D}) \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}}1 \,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^{13} \int_0^{{x}^2} \,dy \,dx= \int_0^{13} y\bigg|_{y=0}^{{x}^2} \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^{13} {x}^2 \,dx= \frac{{x}^3}{3}\bigg|_0^{13}=\frac{13^3}{3} \end{array} Substituting (2) and (3) in (1) we obtain
\overline{H}=\frac{1}{\frac{13^3}{3}}\cdot \frac{13^5}{10}=\frac{3\cdot 13^{2}}{10}=50.7
